title: Workflow Spec
description: The FORWARD CONTRACT for P7's declarative phase workflows (Architecture Review Campaign charter §2 decision 1: workflows-as-data, Claude-as-interpreter; §3 Workflow spec is a Descriptor). A workflow spec is DATA a thinned command reads and Claude interprets — there is no workflow engine on this platform, so this schema is DECLARATIVE ONLY. It describes WHAT a phase requires (entry conditions, ordered stages with their producing agent and artifacts, gates, completion artifacts) and NEVER HOW to control execution. Imperative control-flow fields (retry, rollback, checkpoint, loop, if/then) are explicitly disallowed at every level: rollback is git, resume/checkpoint state is sdlc-context.json, and gates are enforced by hooks — none of that is ever encoded here as if a real engine consumed it (charter §6). No instances exist yet; this defines the shape P7 will author to.
$comment: additionalProperties:false at every level below is what makes the imperative-field ban enforceable: a stray retry/rollback/checkpoint/loop/if/then is rejected as an unknown property wherever it appears, not merely at the root.

name.description: The workflow's identifier — component naming convention, a domain/action noun.

phase.description: The SDLC phase this workflow drives (e.g. 'Design', 'Implement'). One of the eight phases in CLAUDE.md's phase pipeline.

entry_conditions.description: What must already be true before this workflow may begin. Declarative preconditions only — a list of artifacts that must exist and be complete, checked by Claude against sdlc-context.json. Not a guard expression, not control flow.

requires_complete.description: Artifact names (or phase-gate outputs) that must already be complete for entry to be permitted.

stages.description: The ordered stages of the workflow. Ordering plus per-stage depends_on edges declare the dependency graph (charter §6); Claude resolves execution order at runtime. A stage names the single agent that produces its artifacts.

id.description: Stage identifier, unique within the workflow. Referenced by other stages' depends_on and by gates' after/before.

agent.description: The one agent (role-noun, agents/<name>.md) that owns and produces this stage's artifacts. One agent per stage — no overlap (CLAUDE.md Agent Behaviour Rules).

produces.description: The artifact name(s) this stage produces — the same names other stages reference in depends_on and that completion.artifacts_required draws from.

depends_on.description: Stage id(s) that must complete before this stage. Declares an edge in the derived dependency graph — declarative data, not a loop or conditional.

gates.description: Phase/stage gates. Each gate is positioned relative to a stage (after or before) and declares its KIND — a semantic 'approval' (human, e.g. Shafi) or a mechanical 'hook' (deterministic enforcement, charter §6). A gate DECLARES a checkpoint; it never encodes what to do on failure (that is not workflow data — rollback is git, block is a hook exit code).

after.description: Stage id this gate is evaluated after.

before.description: Stage id this gate is evaluated before.

kind.description: 'approval' = a semantic/human gate; 'hook' = a mechanical, deterministic gate enforced by a hook (never by prose).

enforce.description: For a 'hook' kind, the hook name that enforces this gate (e.g. 'pre-phase-advance', 'tdd-gate'). A reference to an enforcer, not an inline rule.

completion.description: What must exist for the workflow to be considered complete — the exit contract. Declarative: a list of required artifacts, checked against sdlc-context.json. Not a control-flow terminator.

artifacts_required.description: Artifact name(s) that must all exist and pass validation for this workflow/phase to be complete.
